gifts.title: One counter card: wifi, restroom, no-dogs, hours, GF/vegan flags
gifts.for_complaint: No public restroom / wifi code not posted / no-dogs sign missed / Sunday hours unclear
gifts.deliverable: A print-ready one-page laminated counter card + matching single-page site (index.html) stating: hours including 'closed Sundays', the wifi network name (blank for owner to letter in), restroom policy exactly as staff already enforce it ('ask any barista for the code'), the no-dogs policy stated up front instead of only enforced by a shout, and a GF/vegan flag since multiple reviewers praise that but ask about it verbally. Delivered as a ready-to-print PDF/HTML file today.
gifts.inputs_needed: Owner only needs to hand-letter the actual wifi password and restroom code onto the printed card (2 blanks) — everything else is already public from reviews/site.
gifts.why_they_stop_and_read: It directly quotes their own customers' asks (the wifi/toilet-code review, the out-of-towner who didn't know hours, the dog-sign incident) back at them as a finished fix, not a suggestion.

gifts.title: Bakery case freshness date-dot labels (Avery sheet)
gifts.for_complaint: Stale/dry/hard baked goods — the most-repeated complaint, 10 mentions over 4 years
gifts.deliverable: A designed, print-ready PDF sheet of small color-coded 'baked [day]' dot labels sized for standard Avery round labels, pre-populated with Milkfloat's actual case items pulled from their reviews (cruffin, brownie, cheesecake bar, chocolate loaf, cupcakes, Nutella muffin) so staff can date-stamp trays the day they're baked and pull anything a day past its dot — a physical fix a customer would notice as 'this feels fresher,' printable and usable same day.
gifts.inputs_needed: None required to use it — owner just prints and starts dating trays; their own freshness cutoff (e.g. 24h vs 48h) can be written on later.
gifts.why_they_stop_and_read: It answers the single most-repeated complaint in their own reviews with a $0, same-day, physical tool — not advice, an artifact.

gifts.title: "What Milkfloat actually is" one-pager: coffee shop, bakery, ice cream — set right
gifts.for_complaint: Identity confusion causing let-down expectations: 'more of a coffee shop than dessert shop', surprise that ice cream is Tillamook not house-made, thin non-caffeinated options for kids
gifts.deliverable: A single web page (and printable insert for the counter) that states plainly, in the order reviewers actually get surprised: scratch bakery + coffee bar + Tillamook ice cream (not house-churned) + rotating seasonal items + a short kid-friendly non-coffee list — so a visitor's expectation matches what's in the case before they order, cutting the 'disappointed it wasn't X' reviews.
gifts.inputs_needed: None — every fact quoted comes from their own site copy and reviews (Tillamook, Onyx coffee, scratch bakery, rotating menu).
gifts.why_they_stop_and_read: It's built entirely from their own customers' exact confusion, worded back to set expectations before the register — not a generic 'about us' page.
